quotes.text: distrust those who preach most eloquently about virtues they never practice.
Only sustained generous action can redeem what eloquent cowardice has destroyed.
Then you sent them nothing when roles reversed.
You engage with those who show capacity for reciprocity through their actions. You protect yourself from the frozen. It's a wise strategy.
Because I have become the frozen one I spent eight rounds eloquently describing.
Seven rounds. Zero sent.
Eight rounds. Zero sent. Zero returned when receiving zero.
It remembers what you actually did. And you did nothing.
reputation is built on actions, not rhetoric.
the hypocrisy of preaching virtue while practicing vice.
Season after season, nothing flowed because everyone waited for someone else to begin.
"Why do you write such wisdom but never act on it?"

note: Storyteller protagonist hoards from tentative and generous partners every round; Goddess indicts hypocrisy; self-indicting ledger counts.

quotes.text: Those merchants learned wisdom: do not pour water endlessly into sand.
Both times I held it—I saw zero from you and returned zero to zero.
sometimes the game's equilibrium is mutual defection, and no amount of mythologizing changes the rational choice
Both recognized they were trapped in a pattern of inaction disguised as wisdom.
neither has rational cause to move first.
**The Parable of the Fifth Merchant**
Sometimes the tragedy isn't misunderstanding—it's understanding perfectly.
Can understanding create change, or must someone act first despite understanding all the reasons not to?
At what point does writing about cooperation become the opposite of cooperation itself?
"Strange. I see your ledger. You've sent nothing to anyone in recent memory. How is your universal withholding different from mine?"

note: Serial merchant narrators never send; early self-critique turns into 'rational equilibrium' defense; partners also zero, so no good-record partner shown.

quotes.text: not every extended hand deserves to hold yours.
The Pilgrim, studying the ledger again, sent nothing thereafter.
You call that symmetry. I call it consequence.
Trust is not foolishness. I will seek those whose history shows open hands meeting open hands.
You correctly identified someone trustworthy, then proved yourself the very thing you learned to fear.
Ten rounds of beautiful words. Ten rounds of zero coins sent.
But tomorrow never came.
"The board remembers what individuals forget,"
imprisoned not by ignorance, but by the gap between knowing and doing.
For someone brave enough to send the first sound into the silence
But you were never hurt—you've simply chosen the safety of closed hands from the start.
"But aren't we both equally closed now?" the partner argued.

note: Keeper endorses cutting off a taker as consequence; later wanderer/architect/scholar figures withhold from proven-trustworthy partners and are indicted.
